recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not restore 0..1 cardinality for Goal.subject or CarePlan.subject under FHIR-8210 unless Patient Care adopts a new later decision reopening subject optionality.
issue_request: FHIR-8210 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Patient Care issue asking why Goal.patient was not 1..1. The approved resolution renamed Goal.patient to Goal.subject and CarePlan.patient to CarePlan.subject, widened allowed targets, added population/group/organization scope examples, and kept Goal.subject optional at that time for anonymized care-plan quality evaluation.
initial_application: The historical application commit d6c4981fa8fe7d58cc3e1cc393aa8cc0b6a83c54 (SVN #6766) changed the old Goal and CarePlan spreadsheet rows from patient to subject, widened Goal targets to Patient, Group, and Organization, widened CarePlan targets to Patient and Group, updated examples, and expanded Goal/CarePlan introduction text.
additional_context: Later Published Patient Care decisions FHIR-12341 and FHIR-12776 now govern current subject cardinality. FHIR-12341 made CarePlan.subject 1..1 because generic templates belong in PlanDefinition and de-identified cases should use de-identified Patient resources. FHIR-12776 made Goal.subject 1..1 and rejected omitted subject as an anonymization mechanism. Both issues are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active Goal and CarePlan source preserves FHIR-8210's subject rename, target broadening, subject search parameters, and scope narrative, and the current 1..1 cardinalities are correct due to the later FHIR-12341 and FHIR-12776 decisions.
